incidents.victim: Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority (LACMTA)
incidents.vector: Network intrusion attributed to a pro-Iran outfit calling itself Ababil of Minab; saboteurs stole 700GB of emails, backups, and files later found inadvertently exposed online.
incidents.impact: March 16 intrusion forced parts of the LA Metro network offline; Israeli researchers at Gambit Security provided forensic evidence linking the attack to Iranian state operations. Same group has hit South Florida's Tri-Rail, vehicle tracker Vyncs, and Saudi infrastructure firm Unimac.

incidents.vector: Misuse of legitimate login credentials assigned to institutions authorized to access state databases; attack likely originated from an unnamed foreign country.
incidents.impact: More than 600,000 records exposed, including names, dates of birth, national ID numbers, and property data. Initial financial damage estimated at €111,000. Centre of Registers chief resigned. Opposition leader alleged Russian intelligence operation hallmarks.

incidents.vector: Phishing email compromised Microsoft 365 email accounts of certain firm personnel; intrusion persisted from July 2024 through June 2025 undetected. Firm allegedly lacked MFA and adequate staff training.
incidents.impact: Stolen data included names, addresses, DOBs, financial accounts, medical information, and Social Security numbers belonging to people who had no relationship with the firm. Victim notifications began March 2026; class action lawsuit filed in DC federal court.

incidents.vector: Zero-day ASP.NET ViewState deserialization (CVE-2026-5426) exploiting hardcoded shared machine keys in the vendor-provided web.config; threat actor deployed an in-memory web shell (Godzilla-style) and used JavaScript tampering to push a fake installer leading to Cobalt Strike infection of site visitors.
incidents.impact: Mandiant confirmed compromise of at least one customer's web server in late 2025; shared keys exposed every internet-facing KnowledgeDeliver instance until rotated. Cobalt Strike payload was custom-prepared for the targeted organization.

incidents.vector: A GitHub employee downloaded a poisoned Visual Studio Code extension distributed as part of the TeamPCP Shai-Hulud npm supply-chain campaign.
incidents.impact: Approximately 4,000 internal private code repositories stolen. TeamPCP took credit; the breach follows the group's release of the Shai-Hulud worm source code, which has spawned copycat activity.

incidents.vector: Network intrusion (details not publicly disclosed) at the largest public health system in the US.
incidents.impact: At least 1.8 million patients affected; stolen data included medical records and biometric information (fingerprints and palm prints) that victims cannot replace.

incidents.attacker: Unknown — insider/contractor exposure (no malicious actor identified)
incidents.vector: A CISA contractor with admin access created a public 'Private-CISA' GitHub profile, disabled GitHub's secret-scanning protection, and committed plaintext credentials including AWS GovCloud keys and an RSA private key for a GitHub app with full access to CISA-IT repos.
incidents.impact: 844MB of sensitive data — passwords, tokens, and CI/CD secrets — exposed publicly since November 2025. More than a week after notification, CISA was still working to invalidate keys; Senate and House lawmakers demanded answers. Researchers warned the exposed key alone enabled rogue self-hosted runners and access to all CISA-IT private repos.

incidents.victim: Stark Industries Solutions / MIRhosting / WorkTitans (hosting providers)
incidents.vector: Dutch FIOD financial crime agency arrested two operators (Andrey Nesterenko, Youssef Zinad) for sanctions evasion after Stark Industries assets were transferred to a successor entity (the.hosting/WorkTitans) following EU sanctions.
incidents.impact: More than 800 servers seized across two Dutch data centers; customer data declared lost. The infrastructure was the most-used network in pro-Russian DDoS attacks on Danish government bodies during Denmark's November 2025 municipal elections, and hosted Doppelgänger disinformation sites.

incidents.victim: Aerospace, defense, and telecom firms (US, Israel, UAE, Middle East)
incidents.vector: Targeted spear-phishing with recruitment lures impersonating global air carriers and video-conferencing brands; DLL sideloading and AppDomainManager hijacking deployed six new RAT variants (MiniUpdate, MiniJunk V2) via Azure-hosted C2 infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 attributes the activity to an Iran-nexus APT (UNC1549). Campaign tempo escalated alongside the Middle East regional conflict that began Feb 28, 2026; samples linked to targets in the US, Israel, UAE, and additional Middle Eastern entities through April 2026.

incidents.victim: Dozens of organizations in North America, Australia, UK (BlackFile victims)
incidents.vector: High-volume voice phishing (vishing) impersonating internal IT with a passkey/MFA pretext; adversary-in-the-middle credential capture against Microsoft 365 and Okta SSO portals, immediate enrollment of attacker-controlled MFA devices, then scripted exfiltration via Microsoft Graph and python-requests using stolen FedAuth cookies.
incidents.impact: Google Threat Intelligence observed exfiltration of more than one million files from a single victim's SharePoint/OneDrive. Group runs a dedicated BlackFile data-leak site, opens with multi-million-dollar demands, and escalates via Gmail spam floods, threatening voicemails to executives, and swatting in severe cases.

incidents.victim: TanStack, OpenSearch, UiPath, Mistral AI, Intercom and 169 other npm packages
incidents.vector: Three-step GitHub Actions abuse chain against TanStack/router: pwn-request via pull_request_target, cache poisoning of the pnpm store, then OIDC token extraction from /proc/<pid>/mem of the runner — publishing malicious npm packages with valid SLSA Build Level 3 provenance and no stolen credentials required.
incidents.impact: Within six minutes 84 malicious package versions published across 42 @tanstack/* packages; by end of day 373 malicious versions across 169 npm packages plus PyPI compromise. Affected packages had ~520 million cumulative downloads in the publish window; @tanstack/react-router alone has 12.7 million weekly downloads. First documented Shai-Hulud-style worm to weaponize SLSA provenance attestation.

incidents.vector: IoT botnet takedown: Canadian authorities arrested a 23-year-old Ottawa man on a US extradition warrant for building and operating Kimwolf, which infected millions of consumer IoT devices.
incidents.impact: Kimwolf launched attacks measured at nearly 30 Tbps — a recorded DDoS record — issued over 25,000 attack commands, caused some victim losses exceeding $1 million, and affected Department of Defense IP ranges. Krebs publicly named the suspect after he doxed and swatted journalists.

incidents.vector: Microsoft civil action and infrastructure seizure: SignSpaceCloud abused the Microsoft Artifact Signing service via hundreds of fake accounts to obtain code-signing certificates that were resold to malware operators.
incidents.impact: Microsoft estimates the service made millions of dollars selling signing certificates to Rhysida, INC, Qilin, Akira, and other ransomware gangs, plus infostealer and SEO-poisoning crews. Domains and servers were seized; service was advertised on Russian Telegram.

incidents.vector: Months-long key-material leakage exploit — likely a cryptographic bug in THORChain's threshold ECDSA implementation allowing a single participant to exfiltrate the secret key.
incidents.impact: Hackers drained one of THORChain's wallets for approximately $10.7 million; the platform suspended crypto trading. Industry researchers flagged the exploit as a failure mode most audits do not model.

incidents.vector: GitHub repository compromise (details not disclosed); ransom note sent demanding payment.
incidents.impact: Grafana confirmed source-code repos were stolen and held for ransom but refused to pay, citing recent FBI guidance against paying attackers. CoinbaseCartel claimed responsibility.

incidents.vector: Misconfigured AWS S3 storage bucket left exposed online without authentication.
incidents.impact: More than one million passport scans and other government IDs from hotel guests left publicly accessible. No confirmed malicious download, but exposure window unknown.

incidents.victim: US gas station operators (automatic tank gauges)
incidents.vector: Suspected Iranian hackers accessed internet-exposed automatic tank gauges that had been left online without passwords.
incidents.impact: Attackers modified fuel-level readings at multiple US gas stations; no fuel-handling accidents reported so far, but the tampering demonstrates continued Iranian targeting of US critical infrastructure exposed via weak authentication.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack (prior incident, financial fallout disclosed this period) that shut down JLR's UK factories for more than a month.
incidents.impact: Annual profit fell 99% to £14 million from £2.5 billion, driven by the cyberattack and US tariffs. JLR stated it expects the worst impact of the cyberattack to have passed.

incidents.vector: Network intrusion (details not disclosed) at the healthcare software vendor handling drug prescriptions for many US clients, including members of Congress.
incidents.impact: Patient prescription data stolen; affected individuals include members of the US Congress. RXNT notified authorities on the final day allowed under US health privacy laws, raising disclosure-timing concerns.

incidents.victim: Pierre & Vacances, Belambra, Gîtes de France
incidents.vector: Network intrusions at three French holiday booking sites; data subsequently put up for sale online.
incidents.impact: Customer data from three major French holiday booking platforms exfiltrated and offered for sale; same actor (ChimeraZ) claimed all three breaches.
